title: 2026 Community Health Needs Assessment
subtitle: AdventHealth Ottawa
cover_note:
AdventHealth Ransom Memorial, Inc. d/b/a AdventHealth Ottawa
Serving Franklin County, Kansas
Draft prepared {{MONTH YEAR}} — pending Hospital Board adoption

blocks.text: AdventHealth Ransom Memorial, Inc. d/b/a AdventHealth Ottawa (referred to in this document as AdventHealth Ottawa or “the Hospital”) conducted a Community Health Needs Assessment (CHNA) in 2026 for the community it serves in Franklin County, Kansas. Building on the Hospital’s 2020 assessment, this CHNA refreshes the community profile with the most recent U.S. Census Bureau data and re-engages community stakeholders to identify and prioritize the area’s most significant health needs.

items: Engage public health and community stakeholders, including low-income, minority and other underserved populations
Assess and understand the community’s current health issues and needs
Understand the health behaviors, risk factors and social determinants that impact health
Identify community resources and collaborate with community partners
Publish the Community Health Needs Assessment and make it widely available to the public
Use the findings to develop and implement a 2027–2029 Community Health Plan based on AdventHealth Ottawa’s prioritized issues

blocks.text: Franklin County is home to an estimated 25,968 residents with a median household income of $68,217 and a poverty rate of 8.3% (U.S. Census Bureau, ACS 2018–2022).

AdventHealth Ottawa is a not-for-profit hospital located in Ottawa, Kansas, the county seat of Franklin County. As part of AdventHealth and in keeping with its mission of Extending the Healing Ministry of Christ, the Hospital provides inpatient, emergency, and outpatient services to residents of Franklin County and surrounding communities.

AdventHealth Ottawa defines its community as Franklin County, Kansas, a predominantly rural county of approximately 572 square miles. The following profile is drawn from the U.S. Census Bureau American Community Survey (ACS) 2018–2022 five-year estimates.

The community is predominantly White (91.8%), with Hispanic or Latino residents representing 4.6%, Black residents 0.6%, and Asian residents 0.5% of the population. The CHNA process included intentional outreach to ensure that low-income, minority and other underserved residents were represented in the community input.
Roughly 22.5% of residents are under age 18 and 19.0% are age 65 and older, reflecting an aging rural population. The county’s 10,185 households have a homeownership rate of approximately 72%.

Consistent with the Hospital’s prior assessments and with IRS section 501(r)(3), AdventHealth Ottawa drew on both primary and secondary data, and solicited input from persons representing the broad interests of the community, including those with public health expertise and those serving medically underserved, low-income and minority populations.

items: Secondary data: U.S. Census Bureau (ACS) demographic and social-determinant indicators, County Health Rankings, and internal hospital utilization data
Primary data: community and stakeholder surveys and key-informant input
Community input: representation from the Hospital, public health partners, and underserved populations

blocks.text: Secondary data highlight several areas where Franklin County trails state or national benchmarks. These indicators, combined with community input, informed the prioritization of significant health needs.

rows: Adults with a bachelor’s degree or higher

blocks.text: Adult obesity (34.2%) and access to primary care remain among the county’s most pressing measured health challenges.

Based on the magnitude and severity of each issue, the feasibility of intervention, and alignment with community input and the Hospital’s capabilities, AdventHealth Ottawa identified the following priority health needs for the 2026 cycle. {{Confirm final priorities with the CHNA Committee.}}

items: Chronic disease and obesity — prevention and management
Access to care — primary care, dental, and specialty services
Behavioral and mental health, including substance use
Social determinants of health — economic stability and healthy food access

blocks.text: AdventHealth Ottawa will present this assessment to its governing body for adoption and will develop a 2027–2029 Community Health Plan with measurable goals and actions for each prioritized need. The Hospital will evaluate progress against the prior cycle and make this report widely available to the public.
Required next step under IRS 501(r)(3): adopt an implementation strategy that maps actions to each prioritized need and evaluates the impact of the prior CHNA.
